newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says PLO-Israel deal is "humiliating".
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says PLO-Israel deal is "humiliating".

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat accepted humiliating terms for a partial Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron, Lebanon's Hizbollah said on Thursday.

"The signing of the Hebron deal did not come as a surprise as much as did the humiliating concessions made by Arafat, including redeployment in Hebron...and illusionary promises empty of any U.S. or Israeli guarantees," the militant Islamic group said in a statement.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Arafat ended months of negotiations on Wednesday by signing a deal that will leave Israel in control of 20 percent of Hebron to protect Jewish settlers.

"The Hebron deal comes as a model for negotiations through which the Zionist enemy aims at getting both land and peace...and points out the pressures and challenges to be faced in the region in the coming period especially on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks," the statement added.

Israeli talks with Lebanon and Syria are deadlocked over an Israeli withdrawal from the Syrian Golan Heights and a south Lebanon occupation zone. Syria arms Hizbollah guerrillas who are fighting to oust Israeli troops from the 15-km (nine mile)-deep border occupation zone.
Hizbollah said the Hebron deal, the latest stage in the Oslo peace process begun in 1993, was part of a plan to consolidate Jewish settlements on Palestinian territories.
"This deal is a renewed betrayal committed by Arafat since he collapsed in front of U.S.-Israeli will and signed the treacherous Oslo agreement in September 1993," the statement said.
